title: Arrow-Wilf equivalences and enumerative results for short arrow patterns
summary: Arrow patterns, introduced by Berman and Tenner, provide a unified framework for studying permutation classes where both one-line and cycle structure constraints are present. In this paper, we continue the systematic study of arrow pattern avoidance initiated by Archer and Laudone. We establish several structural results, including a key lemma that translates arrow patterns into vincular patterns under certain conditions, and derive a series of arrow-Wilf equivalences arising from reversal, complementation, and insertion operations.
